scaleControls.description: Guide p22 drawing: the CMDU bezel is 100 by 138 px of a 717 px panel. Lockheed's 8 x 11 in CMDU therefore gives 1.456 m, and the standby attitude bezel comes out at 85 mm against a 3 in indicator. The earlier 2.12 m estimate was 1.46 times too large.

overlays.scope: Four CMDUs, standby instruments, shelf and lower controls. Absolute panel scale remains estimated.

corrections: Replaced the generic transport with an unstretched C-130J: raised flight deck and blunt nose, constant cargo barrel, upswept ramp, high unswept-leading-edge wing, tapered horizontal tail, tall fin and separate wheel sponsons.

Rebuilt four long J nacelles with recessed intake/exhaust details, six swept blades on each independent propeller, twin nose wheels and four tandem main wheels. Selected shell/wing seams and rivets follow actual surface facets.

Corrected the prototype six-screen cockpit to the manufacturer four-CMDU layout, with standby instruments, upper avionics shelf, blank optional bay, lower hydraulic/gear modules, dual roof-mounted HUD structures, three console CNI controllers and four power levers.

Overlay iterations shortened the horizontal-tail chord and refined its taper. Sightline testing moved the obstructing wiper. Control tests fixed swept-hinge mount orientation and separated propeller mesh names from cockpit NP gauges.

Both pilot displays share telemetry expressions; all four NP gauges read their own engine state. Wired attitude, true heading, true airspeed, geometric altitude, vertical speed, flap/gear indications, yokes, pedals, throttles, flaps, ailerons, elevators and rudder. Unsupported engine/navigation systems remain unavailable.
reviewNotes.independentDimensions: USAF T.O.00-105E-9 C-130J.2: standard-body 97ft9in /29.79m, wingspan132ft7in /40.41m, tail52ft8in /16.05m, bodyheight16ft1in /4.90m, maintrack14ft3in /4.34m, nosegear3.50m behind nose and tandem-main spacing1.524m. Propellers nominal13ft6in /4.115m. Height11.84m follows manufacturer guide (rescue drawing labels38ft11in). Uniform view scales reveal schematic inconsistencies; cockpit width2.12m is an estimate, not a certified measured station.
reviewNotes.visual: Personally inspected four final-hash overlays, eight standard views and twelve detail/state captures. Checked zero/cruise/limits/negative-altitude/missing telemetry, different NP values including a stopped fourth engine, overhead, pedestal, clean gear-up exterior and both control extremes. All23 shared instrument tests and final targeted geometry/cardinal/hinge checks passed; separate deterministic candidate is byte-identical.
limitations: The Air Force dimensional drawing is a low-resolution schematic: front fin height, top-view length and printed prop-to-nose dimension disagree with the independent dimensions and other views. The model uses consistent overall dimensions; overlay alignment is not an engineering-tolerance claim.

Body sections, cockpit scale and depth, nacelle contours and glass frames are estimated from drawings and photographs. The simplified seats, sidewalls, overhead controls and lower panel do not reproduce every switch or installation variation.

CMDU symbology is an original simulator adaptation. Readings are true airspeed, geometric altitude and true heading; no pitot/static, magnetic, radio/navigation, HUD collimation, terrain map or autopilot simulation is implied.

NP displays use each simulated engine normalized rotor speed, not a detailed constant-speed propeller governor. Torque, ITT, gas-generator speed, oil, fuel, hydraulics, bleed-air and failures have no modeled telemetry and remain blank/INOP.

Gear retracts by simplified translation and hiding; flaps rotate without full Fowler-track extension. Cargo ramp stays closed; cargo furnishings, optional tanks, mission equipment and external weapons are omitted. Seams/fasteners are selective rather than a manufacturing rivet schedule.

cockpitPass.problem: The side view showed the crown up to 0.7 m low at z 12.4 and the whole window block and flight deck about 1.5 m too far aft. The eye had been raised to clear that nose, leaving 1.15 m above the cushion. The flat slab was a glareshield box stopping 0.6 m short of the wall. The black box on legs in the middle of the windscreen was the pilot's HUD: projector and two struts drawn at 0.7 m ahead of the eye, at 0.67 m lateral.
corrections: Forebody re-traced from the pocket guide p20 side and plan views and checked on the ZH883 photograph: new smooth forebody, level sill at 3.5 m, row divider, top rail, centre pane between two posts, side windows ending at z 11.95 as drawn, not 9.25.
Flight deck moved 1.5 m forward. Eye lowered 0.36 m to 3.97 m, which sits 0.79 m over the existing cushion on the existing 2.72 m floor, so seat and floor were right and the eye was the error.

Panel scaled by 0.687 from the 8 x 11 in CMDU. Slab replaced by one flat hood meeting the skin below the glass, with blanking panels to the walls. Console scaled 0.8 and overhead 0.85 from the guide; the overhead is now tilted along the roof, and pilots moved inboard to 0.55 m so they sit on their displays.
HUDs rebuilt from the RAF photograph: a roof projector beside the overhead, a thin C-arm, and a 200 x 160 mm combiner 0.33 m ahead of each eye. Static and deployed; no symbology is drawn or implied.
cockpitPass.visual: Inspected the runtime seat view (dead ahead, 60 degrees vertical), look-down, look-right and an aisle view, plus exterior front, both quarters, low and side, after the final rebuild. Rays fanned from above over the nose and roof hit only skin, glass and exterior frames.
cockpitPass.assumptions: The eye's z comes from the side window position in the guide and photographs, and its height from the existing floor and cushion; no published C-130J design eye or flight deck floor height was found.

The model uses consistent overall dimensions; overlay alignment is not an engineering-tolerance claim.

Body sections, cockpit scale and depth, nacelle contours and glass frames are estimated from drawings and photographs. The simplified seats, sidewalls, overhead controls and lower panel do not reproduce every switch or installation variation.

CMDU symbology is an original simulator adaptation. Readings are true airspeed, geometric altitude and true heading; no pitot/static, magnetic, radio/navigation, HUD collimation, terrain map or autopilot simulation is implied.

NP displays use each simulated engine normalized rotor speed, not a detailed constant-speed propeller governor. Torque, ITT, gas-generator speed, oil, fuel, hydraulics, bleed-air and failures have no modeled telemetry and remain blank/INOP.

The lower cheek windows beside the rudder pedals are not modeled; the front panes are curved on the skin rather than flat; and the HUD combiner is plain glass, always deployed, with no symbology. Flight deck stations are reconstructed from a small manufacturer drawing and photographs, and the panel outboard of the display block is blank.
